payload.claim: No test in this diff ever exercises a successful resolution where the second candidate — the predecessor's recorded head, `row["predecessor_head"]` — is the one actually chosen as the base. Every scenario that reaches `_layer_candidates`'s predecessor branch (restacked-child 'B', unmoved chain 'D', gone-branch 'C'/'key_child'/'key_mid') either succeeds on the first candidate (`fetch(predecessor_branch)` or `own_parent`) or fails on both and asserts only the error message. Deleting the fallback — changing line 233 to `return [fetch(predecessor_branch)], None` — would make a layer whose predecessor's branch still exists but has moved ahead of what the layer was actually built from (the ordinary 'review commit landed on the parent, child was never rebased' case this whole spec exists to handle) raise `ValueError` instead of correctly resolving to the predecessor's recorded head, yet every test in `tests/test_end_review.py` and `tests/test_cli.py` would still pass. This directly contradicts acceptance criterion 1's explicit claim that 'A layer that was not restacked starts at its predecessor's recorded head,' which the `criteria: pass` gate result renders as satisfied.
